note: The community type (basics.type): the kind of group, e.g. family, workplace, movement, one per card, plus Other. Required in set-up; public from Misty; shapes suggestions (type_value_fit.json, type_approach_fit.json). Renamed 2026-10-09 from settings.json; the online space is now formats.json. status: proposed until reviewed.

items.label: Personal space
items.description: Run by one person, for themselves and whoever they let in.
items.examples: A single-user Mastodon or Bluesky server, a personal blog with comments, someone's own small Discord

items.label: Family
items.description: Relatives keeping in touch and organizing family life.
items.examples: A family group chat, a cousins' Discord, a shared family calendar

items.label: Friends
items.description: A group of friends, or friends of friends.
items.examples: A friend group's chat, a weekly games night, a running club of friends

items.label: Neighborhood / local
items.description: People who live in the same place.
items.examples: A street or building forum, a neighborhood mutual aid chat, a village noticeboard

items.label: Civic / public
items.description: Public life: residents, citizens, local government.
items.examples: A participatory budgeting forum, a public consultation, a citizens' assembly

items.label: Workplace / organization
items.description: People who work together in one organization.
items.examples: A company's Slack, a nonprofit's staff chat, a team's workspace

items.label: Professional / industry
items.description: People in the same field, across organizations.
items.examples: A professional network, an industry mailing list, a practitioners' Slack

items.label: Classroom / education
items.description: Learners and teachers in a course or school.
items.examples: A class forum, a course's Discord, a school club

items.label: Movement / activism
items.description: People organizing for a cause or for change.
items.examples: A tenants' union, a climate campaign, a mutual aid network

items.label: Hobby / interest / fandom
items.description: People who share an interest.
items.examples: A gardening server, a knitting forum, a fandom community

items.label: Open source / peer production
items.description: People making something together in the open.
items.examples: An open-source project, a wiki, a shared map or dataset

items.label: Faith / spiritual
items.description: A religious or spiritual community.
items.examples: A parish mailing list, a meditation group, a congregation's chat

items.label: Research / science
items.description: Researchers working together.
items.examples: A lab's chat, a research collaboration, a research network

items.label: Citizen science
items.description: Members of the public collecting, classifying or analyzing data for a research project. Often run by scientists or an institution, but also by communities and collectives.
items.examples: A Zooniverse project, iNaturalist, a bird count, a community air-quality network

items.label: General-purpose social space
items.description: A public space for many kinds of people, not one group: general feeds and servers.
items.examples: A general Mastodon or Bluesky community, a general-interest server, an open public forum

items.label: Support / peer support
items.description: People supporting each other through something.
items.examples: A recovery group, a patient community, a grief or caregivers' group

items.label: Cooperative / collective
items.description: Owned and run by its members.
items.examples: A worker co-op, a housing co-op, a platform co-op, an artists' collective

items.label: Club / association
items.description: A membership organization with formal members.
items.examples: A sports club, an alumni association, a membership nonprofit

items.label: Identity / cultural community
items.description: People who share an identity or culture.
items.examples: A diaspora group, an LGBTQ+ space, a language community, etc.

items.label: Creator and audience
items.description: A community around a creator or a small team.
items.examples: A streamer's Discord, a newsletter's readers, a podcast community

items.label: DAO / web3 project
items.description: An organization governed on a blockchain.
items.examples: A protocol DAO, a grants DAO, a token-governed project
